mentions.name: Personal feed curation for events+more
mentions.description: This system curates a personal feed of events and more by ingesting multiple streams of information, such as event calendars, newsletters, and social streams like Facebook groups and Instagram, so users don't have to visit those apps directly. It uses LLMs for use-cases where the user controls what is done on their behalf.
mentions.problem: People have lost control over their email inboxes and information streams over the last decade, and information like event calendars or Facebook/Instagram groups sits in apps they'd rather not open directly.
mentions.audience: Individuals who want to control what is done on their behalf across their information streams.
mentions.source_excerpt:
Personal feed curation for events+more.

It feels like somewhere in the last decade we've all lost control over our email inboxes. While it would certainly be possible to filter and sort it, I've been wondering if it makes sense to just start with a system that is designed to intake a bunch of streams of information.
